original_question: The thickness of a bar k-visibility graph is known to be at most 2k(9k - 1). Improve this upper bound.
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Open Problem 24: "It has been shown that the thickness of a bar k-visibility graph is bounded by 2k(9k-1). Can this upper bound be improved?"
correct_elements: Your draft targets the correct object (bar k-visibility graphs), the correct parameter (thickness), the correct cited upper bound 2k(9k-1), and the correct research direction: improving that bound.
missing_details: It does not define what a bar k-visibility graph is: a graph admitting a strong bar-visibility representation by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars in the plane, where two vertices are adjacent exactly when some vertical sightline between their bars intersects at most k other bars.
It does not define thickness: the minimum number of planar graphs whose union is the graph.
It does not state the quantifiers explicitly: the question is about a universal upper bound for every bar k-visibility graph, as a function of the integer parameter k.
For the quoted bound 2k(9k-1), one should specify that the relevant regime is k >= 1; bar 0-visibility graphs are the ordinary bar visibility graphs.
It does not make fully explicit that the task is to improve the general worst-case upper bound, not to settle a special subclass or a single instance.

To stay paper-faithful, it should not be reformulated as proving thickness at most 2 or determining the exact maximum thickness, since the surrounding discussion only asks for improvement of the known upper bound.
refined_question: For each integer k >= 1, find a universal function f(k) with f(k) < 2k(9k-1) such that every bar k-visibility graph G has thickness theta(G) <= f(k), where G is a bar k-visibility graph if it admits a strong visibility representation by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars in the plane in which two vertices are adjacent if and only if there exists a vertical sightline between their bars that intersects at most k other bars, and where theta(G) is the minimum number of planar graphs whose union is G.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. In Section 3.3, after defining bar k-visibility graphs and recalling the notion of thickness, the survey states Open Problem 24 asking whether the known upper bound on the thickness of a bar k-visibility graph can be improved. The immediately preceding paragraph gives the needed scope: the problem concerns the class of bar k-visibility graphs, thickness as a planarity measure, and the specific upper bound 2k(9k-1) attributed to Dean et al. The same paragraph also notes that a stronger thickness-at-most-2 conjecture was disproved, so the faithful sharpening is to ask only for a better general upper bound, not for an exact value or for thickness 2. I therefore kept your question narrowly centered on improving the universal bound, while making the definitions and quantifiers explicit so that the question stands alone.
